name: King's Gambit (Kieseritzky)
line: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ne5 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5 Bd6 d4
idea: Give the f-pawn to rip open the f-file and get a big centre. Your targets are f7 and the black king. Don't rush — get castled, then bring the rook to f1 and the bishop to c4 aimed at f7.

name: Evans Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 exd4 O-O
idea: Throw in b4 to deflect the c5 bishop, then c3 and d4 win time and build a big centre. Your bishops on c4 and (later) a3 or b2 slice towards the castled king. Rapid development is the whole point.

name: Danish Gambit
line: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Bc4 cxb2 Bxb2 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Bxf7+
idea: Give up two pawns for two bishops raking the board from c4 and b2. Black's f7 and g7 are under fire before Black can develop. Very sharp: know the defence 4...d5 and keep attacking.

name: Scotch Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Bc4 Nf6 e5 d5 Bb5 Ne4 Nxd4 Bd7 Bxc6 bxc6 O-O
idea: Leave the d4 pawn and develop with Bc4. If Black grabs with ...Nf6, push e5 and kick the knight. You get the initiative and easy piece play.

name: Göring Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Bb4 Bc4 d6 O-O Bxc3 bxc3 Nf6 e5
idea: A Danish-style pawn sacrifice from the Scotch. You trade a pawn for fast development, the open d-file and pressure on f7.

name: Smith-Morra Gambit
line: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 d6 Bc4 e6 O-O Nf6 Qe2 Be7 Rd1
idea: The anti-Sicilian pawn sac: open c- and d-files, Bc4, Qe2, rooks to c1 and d1. Black is cramped and the d6 pawn becomes a target. Watch out for the Siberian Trap (see below).

name: Vienna Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 Nxe4 Nf3 Be7 d4 O-O Bd3
idea: A King's Gambit with Nc3 played first. After fxe5 you gain space on the kingside and use the half-open f-file to attack.

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
line: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 c6 Be3
idea: 1.d4 players' wild weapon: give the e-pawn and f-pawn for open lines, a lead in development and an attack down the f-file.

name: Fried Liver Attack
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+ Ke6 Nc3 Nb4 a3 Nxc2+ Kd1 Nxa1 Nxd5
idea: If Black recaptures 5...Nxd5, sacrifice the knight on f7 to drag the king into the middle. Qf3+ and Nc3 pile on the pinned d5 knight. Huge fun at club level.

name: Staunton Gambit
line: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6 d5 Ne5 Qd4
idea: Hit the Dutch straight away: give the e-pawn, develop fast and target e4 and the weakened kingside.

name: Halloween Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe5 d4 Ng6 e5 Ng8 Bc4
idea: Give a whole knight for a big pawn centre that chases Black's knights back home. Objectively dubious, practically dangerous under 1500.

name: Stafford Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Be2 h5
idea: Give a pawn in the Petrov for open lines and a quick attack with ...Bc5, ...Ng4 and ...h5. Full of traps against natural moves.

name: Englund Gambit
line: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Qd5 f6 exf6 Nxf6
idea: An offbeat answer to 1.d4. The pawn usually comes back, and many players walk straight into the queen trap (below).

name: Budapest Gambit
line: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 Nc6 Nf3 Bb4+ Nbd2 Qe7 e3 Ngxe5
idea: Hit back at the Queen's Gambit with ...e5. You usually win the e5 pawn back with ...Ng4, ...Nc6 and ...Qe7, with active pieces.

name: Albin Countergambit
line: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 g3 Be6 Nbd2 Qd7
idea: The d4 pawn becomes a bone in White's throat. Castle queenside and attack the kingside with ...Bh3 and pawn storms.

name: Benko Gambit
line: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6 bxa6 Bxa6 Nc3 d6 e4 Bxf1 Kxf1 g6
idea: A long-term pawn sacrifice: open a- and b-files for your rooks, put the bishop on g7 and press the queenside forever.

name: Marshall Attack
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5 c6
idea: Grandmaster gambit against the Ruy López. Give the e5 pawn, then swing ...Bd6, ...Qh4 and ...Bg4 at White's king.

name: Traxler Counterattack
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2+ Kxf2 Nxe4+
idea: Answer the Fried Liver setup by ignoring the threat: ...Bc5! and when White takes on f7, sacrifice on f2 and attack the exposed king.

name: Schliemann Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5
idea: A King's Gambit with colours reversed against the Ruy López. Fight for e4 and play for the open f-file.

name: Latvian Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 Nxe5 Qf6 d4 d6 Nc4 fxe4
idea: The wildest reply to 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3. Objectively risky, but it drags opponents into chaos from move two.

name: Elephant Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 e4 Qe2 Nf6 d3
idea: Strike in the centre at once. Black aims for quick development and tricks on the e-file.

name: Icelandic Gambit
line: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4 e6 dxe6 Bxe6
idea: In the Scandinavian, give a pawn for a big lead in development and pressure on White's centre.

name: Stafford trap: Bg5?? Nxe4!
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Bg5 Nxe4 Bxd8 Bxf2+ Ke2 Bg4#
idea: White pins the knight with Bg5. Ignore the 'pin' — take e4 and let them grab your queen.
note: After Bxd8, Bxf2+ and Bg4# is mate. The famous 'Oh no, my queen!' trap.

name: Englund trap
line: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Bc3 Bb4 Qd2 Bxc3 Qxc3 Qc1#
idea: After Bf4, the check on b4 forks king and b2. Natural moves by White lose on the spot.
note: Qc1# — the queen and the pinned knight on b1 leave the white king nowhere to go.

name: Lasker trap (Albin)
line: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2 dxe3 Bxb4 exf2+ Ke2 fxg1=N+ Rxg1 Bg4+
idea: White grabs the bishop on b4, but the pawn on e3 is unstoppable.
note: Underpromotion to a knight with check, then Bg4+ wins the queen. One of the prettiest traps in chess.

name: Budapest trap: axb4?? Nd3#
line: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 Nc6 Nf3 Bb4+ Nbd2 Qe7 a3 Ngxe5 axb4 Nd3#
idea: White kicks the bishop with a3 and grabs it — but the e5 knight jumps in.
note: Nd3# is a smothered mate: the white king is boxed in by its own pieces.

name: Siberian trap (vs Morra)
line: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 e6 Bc4 Qc7 O-O Nf6 Qe2 Ng4 h3 Nd4 Nxd4 Qh2#
idea: How Black punishes careless Smith-Morra play: ...Ng4 eyes h2, and after h3 the knight jumps to d4 hitting the queen.
note: If White takes the knight, Qh2# — if the queen moves, Qh2# anyway.

name: Fried Liver: queen hunt
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+ Ke6 Nc3 Nb4 Qe4 c6 d4
idea: Black defends the knight with ...Nb4 instead of ...Ncb4. Keep the king in the centre and open lines with d4.
note: With d4, the e5 pawn falls and the black king has no shelter. Your lead in development is decisive.

name: Legal's mate
line: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 Bc4 Bg4 Nc3 g6 Nxe5 Bxd1 Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5#
idea: Black pins your knight to the queen with ...Bg4. Break the pin by force: give the queen.
note: Bxf7+ and Nd5# — three minor pieces mate the king.

name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxe5 Qg5 Nxf7 Qxg2 Rf1 Qxe4+ Be2 Nf3#
idea: A cheeky trap for Black: ...Nd4 looks like a blunder that drops e5. If White grabs it, Black's queen and knight crash in.
note: Nf3# — smothered on e2. Objectively ...Nd4 is dubious, so use it as a surprise, not a main weapon.
